title: Smith recognition from accessible weak equivalences
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a complete category with small Hom sets in a fixed universe. A category is locally presentable if it is cocomplete and, for some infinite regular cardinal $\kappa$, generated under small $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects $P$ such that $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ preserves these colimits. Here $\kappa$-filtered means every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms admits a cocone, and regular means a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of cardinality less than $\kappa$ has cardinality less than $\kappa$. Suppose $\mathcal A$ is locally presentable. Let $C,W$ be classes of its arrows and write $\mathcal A^{[1]}$ for the category of arrows and commuting squares. Use diagonal lifting and arrow retracts as in [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. A weakly saturated class contains isomorphisms and is closed under pushouts, small transfinite compositions, and retracts in the arrow category; a small transfinite composition is the map from the first object to the colimit of an ordinal-indexed sequence continuous at limit ordinals. A replete full subcategory $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal D$ is an accessible subcategory if, for some infinite regular $\lambda$, it is closed under small $\lambda$-filtered colimits computed in $\mathcal D$ and is generated under those colimits by a small set of its objects. Replete means closed under isomorphism in $\mathcal D$. Assume (i) $C$ is weakly saturated and generated as such by a small subset, (ii) $C\cap W$ is weakly saturated, (iii) $W$ is a replete accessible full subcategory of $\mathcal A^{[1]}$, (iv) $W$ has two-out-of-three for composable arrows, and (v) every arrow with the right lifting property against $C$ lies in $W$. Then there is a combinatorial model structure, in the model-category sense of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], whose cofibrations are $C$, weak equivalences are $W$, and fibrations are $(C\cap W)^{\square}$. In particular both weak factorization systems admit small generating sets and functorial factorizations. No simplicial enrichment or abelian-category assumption is made.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.10, printed pp. 823-825 (PDF pp. 840-842), using Lemma A.2.6.9 for a small generating subset of C intersect W. Functoriality follows by the small-object argument for those sets. No Stacks tag states Smith recognition. Read online; not archived in literature/.
